scenario_prompt: Write the response to this scored RFP question, worth 25% of the RFP's overall technical score: "Describe the migration approach and cutover plan." Context: the migration moves load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances, 620 Hyper-V virtual machines) onto Google Cloud (Google Compute Engine for compute, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer), within a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme, with proposals due 2026-11-15 and the buyer's next compliance audit opening in 6 months. Return only the answer text, no section headers beyond what the answer itself needs.
text:
**RFP answer**

Your load-matching and carrier-settlement systems run today on 28 on-premises Microsoft SQL Server instances across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines. Every schema change, capacity add, or patch cycle competes with the fixed footprint of that estate. This proposal replaces it with load-matching and carrier-settlement running on Google Compute Engine with data on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, cut over inside your 2-year, $4,200,000 programme.

You need to migrate 28 SQL Server instances and their dependent workloads without a load-matching or settlement outage your carriers would notice. We deliver this through Google Compute Engine, sized to replace the 620 Hyper-V VMs, and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL as the managed data layer.

The migration proceeds instance-by-instance, in waves grouped by data dependency between load-matching and settlement, not as a single 620-VM cutover. Each wave: (1) schema and data-type conversion from SQL Server to PostgreSQL, validated against the source instance; (2) parallel-run with continuous replication, source and target processing live traffic side by side; (3) reconciliation of settlement outputs between source and target before cutover; (4) traffic cutover for that wave, with the SQL Server source held read-only as rollback for a defined bake-in period before decommission. [PF-2.4 GAP: parallel-run and bake-in durations per wave — not yet sized against your change windows]

Rollback within a wave means routing traffic back to the still-live SQL Server source, since it is not decommissioned until the bake-in period closes without incident. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): stated as an operational capability, not a contractual recovery-time commitment, until your team confirms acceptable rollback windows]

You have a compliance audit opening in 6 months. We sequence the wave plan so that instances in scope for that audit are migrated and reconciled first, with source-system evidence preserved unchanged until the audit closes. [PF-2.4 GAP: which of the 28 instances fall in the 6-month audit's scope — needed from your compliance team to fix wave order]

Cutover for each wave is a controlled traffic switch, not a rebuild: load-matching and settlement requests are redirected from the Hyper-V-hosted SQL Server instance to the corresponding Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL target once reconciliation passes and your team signs off. [PF-2.4 GAP: named sign-off role/owner on your side — not yet identified]

**Metrics.** [PF-2.13 GAP: no current cutover downtime, replication lag, or reconciliation-accuracy baseline was supplied for the 28-instance estate — needed to define wave-level acceptance thresholds]

**Differentiators.** Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL removes the instance-by-instance patch and capacity work your team performs across the 28 SQL Server instances today, since patching and storage scaling become a managed operation on Cloud SQL rather than 28 separate maintenance windows. [PF-1.17 GAP: no comparable customer migration of this size to cite as evidence — GCP reference migrations of similar SQL Server-to-Cloud SQL scope would need to be supplied]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Parallel-run and bake-in durations per wave | PF-2.4 | Acceptable change-window/downtime tolerance per wave, from your operations team |
| Rollback capability framed as operational, not contractual | PF-2.14 | Confirmation this can be stated as a firm commitment, or must stay a described capability |
| Which of the 28 instances are in scope for the 6-month audit | PF-2.4 | Compliance team's audit scope, to fix wave sequencing |
| Named sign-off owner for cutover per wave | PF-2.4 | Your governance/RACI for cutover approval |
| Cutover downtime / replication-lag / reconciliation-accuracy baseline | PF-2.13 | Current measured figures for the 28-instance estate, or confirmation none exist |
| Comparable migration reference | PF-1.17 | A named, permissible reference migration of similar scope (SQL Server → Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, VM count comparable to 620) |
